org.portico.utils.messaging

Class Module

  • java.lang.Object
    • org.portico.utils.messaging.Module

  • public class Module
extends Object
    A Module collects together IMessageHandler classes so that they can be stored as a single unit and applied to a MessageSink or group of sinks as a single unit. Each Module has a name that a IMessageHandler should specify in its MessageHandler annotation to associate it with the module. You can apply a set of MessageSinks to a Module and have each contained handler be added to the appropriate sinks.

      • apply

        public Set<Class<?>> apply(MessageSink[] sinks,
                           String[] keywords,
                           Map<String,Object> properties)
                    throws MessagingException
        Create a new instance of each of the handler classes contained in the module and adds them to the appropriate MessageSinks from the set given to this method as a parameter.

        Which handlers are applied to which sinks?

        For each IMessageHandler class in the Module, the declared MessageHandler annotation is located. The MessageSinks that this handler wants to be applied to are extracted from the annotation and then located in the group of sinks (by name) that were passed to this call. If the handler annotation declares a sink that doesn't exist in the given set, an exception is thrown.

        Each handler can be registered multiple times with a single MessageSink (once for each of the PorticoMessage types it declared. For each sink a handler wants to be registered with, a new instance of the handler class will be created and registered using all the message types it declares (in MessageHandler.messages()). To repeat, for each sink a new handler instance is created, but, that same instance is used more than once (for the sink) if the handler wants to handle more than one message type. Thus, the same handler can be registered multiple times with a single sink, but if the handler declared multiple sinks, there will be a separate instance for each sink. Gots it?

        If the MessageHandler indicates that it is a global handler, the messages are ignored and a new instance is created and registered with the sink only as a global handler.

        Restricting Handlers With Keywords

        In the MessageHandler annotation, each handler can specify a set of keywords that must be provided before applying it to the given set of sinks. This allows components to provide some form of identification (perhaps a name or a list of capabilities) and for handlers within a module to opt-in or out of being applied. If at least one of the requested keywords provided by the handler does not match at least one of the keywords provided to the call, that handler will not be applied. If the handler provides no keywords, or there are no keywords provided to the call, then all handlers will be applied (no keywords is effectively the same as saying "all keywords").

        Parameters:
        sinks - The group of sinks that the handlers contained in this Module can be applied to.
        keywords - The set of keywords that should match up with the Message Handler keywords if the handler is to be applied to the sinks (see above).
        Returns:
        The set of handlers that were successfully applied to at least one of the sinks
        Throws:
        MessagingException - If a handler wants a MessageSink that isn't in the set that was passed. If the IMessageHandler class can't be instantiated. If there is a problem registering a handler with a sink.

      • findModules

        public static Collection<Module> findModules(URL location)
                                      throws JConfigurationException
        This method will scan the jar file at the given location for all classes containing the MessageHandler annotation. It will then sort each of the found handlers into separate Modules which are then returned.

        Should handlers for a single module be spread across multiple jar files (quite likely), you can pass in a collection of existing modules that will be returned. If the given collection is null, this is automatically converted to an empty collection, so null is a valid value. Note that the original collection will NOT be altered. A new, updated collection will be returned.

        Parameters:
        fromPath - The jar-file to scan for any classes that declare the MessageHandler annotation
        existing - The collection of existing modules you want to update. Null will cause a new collection to be automatically created. Note that the origin collection will not be altered, a new, updated collection will be returned
        Throws:
        JConfigurationException
